crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The analyzed binary is a legitimate 7-Zip Uninstaller (version 24.09). Its behavior is consistent with standard software removal procedures, including: 1) Copying itself to a temporary directory (%TEMP%\7z*.tmp\Uninst.exe) to allow for the deletion of the primary installation folder; 2) Removing application files and language packs via DeleteFileW; 3) Cleaning up registry entries under HKLM and HKCU, specifically 'Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\7-Zip', 'App Paths', and shell extension CLSIDs ({23170F69-40C1-278A-1000-000100020000}); and 4) Deleting start menu shortcuts and directories using SHGetFolderPathW and RemoveDirectoryW. It correctly handles in-use files using MoveFileExW with the MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT flag.
